back: A network over a small area, such as a building, owned and managed by one organisation.
A network over a large area, usually using links leased from carriers; the internet is the largest.
Dedicated servers provide services (files, print, email, login) to client computers; managed centrally.
Computers have equal status and each can be both client and server; no dedicated server.
Central security and backups; easy to manage many users. Drawbacks: server cost, a skilled administrator, and a single point of failure.
Cheap and simple; no administrator. Drawbacks: weak security, no central backup, hard to manage when large.
A computer with little processing power or storage that relies on a server for processing; needs a connection.
A full computer with its own processor, storage and software; does its own processing and works offline.
